title: Acts Chapter 21 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 21 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 21 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 21.

questions.question: In Acts 21, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: We came with a straight course unto Coos
Paul was told not to go up to Jerusalem
We entered into the house of Philip the evangelist
Agabus bound his hands and feet with Paul's girdle
questions.correctAnswer: We came with a straight course unto Coos
questions.explanation: Acts 21:1 states we came with a straight course unto Coos at the beginning of the chapter, before the other events.

questions.question: To which island did they sail after Coos and Rhodes according to Acts 21?
questions.correctAnswer: Patara
questions.explanation: Acts 21:1 states they came unto Coos, then Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara.

questions.question: What kind of ship did they find in Acts 21:2?
options: A ship sailing over unto Phenicia
questions.correctAnswer: A ship sailing over unto Phenicia
questions.explanation: Acts 21:2 says they found a ship sailing over unto Phenicia and went aboard.

questions.question: Where did the ship unload her burden according to Acts 21?
questions.correctAnswer: Tyre
questions.explanation: Acts 21:3 states the ship was to unload her burden at Tyre.

questions.question: How long did Paul and the disciples tarry at Tyre?
questions.correctAnswer: Seven days
questions.explanation: Acts 21:4 states they tarried there seven days.

questions.question: What warning did the disciples at Tyre give Paul through the Spirit?
options: He should not go up to Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: He should not go up to Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Acts 21:4 says the disciples told Paul through the Spirit not to go up to Jerusalem.

questions.question: Who did Paul and his companions stay with in Caesarea?
questions.correctAnswer: Philip the evangelist
questions.explanation: Acts 21:8 states they entered into the house of Philip the evangelist in Caesarea.

questions.question: How many daughters did Philip have who prophesied?
questions.correctAnswer: Four
questions.explanation: Acts 21:9 says Philip had four daughters who did prophesy.

questions.question: What did the prophet Agabus do with Paul's girdle?
options: Bound his own hands and feet with it
Gave it to Paul as a gift
Used it to tie the ship's sail
questions.correctAnswer: Bound his own hands and feet with it
questions.explanation: Acts 21:11 states Agabus took Paul's girdle and bound his own hands and feet with it.

questions.question: What did Agabus say would happen to Paul at Jerusalem?
options: The Jews at Jerusalem would bind him and deliver him to the Gentiles
He would be welcomed with gifts
He would sail back to Caesarea
questions.correctAnswer: The Jews at Jerusalem would bind him and deliver him to the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Acts 21:11 quotes Agabus saying the Jews at Jerusalem will bind Paul and deliver him to the Gentiles.

questions.question: How did Paul respond to those who begged him not to go to Jerusalem?
options: He said he was ready to be bound and even to die at Jerusalem
He agreed to stay away from Jerusalem
He said he would go to Rome instead
He said he would go to Tyre
questions.correctAnswer: He said he was ready to be bound and even to die at Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Acts 21:13 records Paul saying he is ready not only to be bound but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.

questions.question: What did they say when Paul would not be persuaded to avoid going to Jerusalem?
options: The will of the Lord be done
Let us all go with him
questions.correctAnswer: The will of the Lord be done
questions.explanation: Acts 21:14 states when Paul would not be persuaded, they ceased saying, The will of the Lord be done.

questions.question: Paul and his companions kneeled down on the shore and prayed before taking ship at Tyre.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 21:5 states they kneeled down on the shore and prayed before taking ship.

questions.question: Agabus came down from Judaea to Caesarea while Paul was staying there.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 21:10 says a certain prophet named Agabus came down from Judaea while they were in Caesarea.

questions.question: According to Acts 21, Paul was persuaded by the disciples not to go to Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 21:14 states Paul would not be persuaded to avoid going to Jerusalem.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 21 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 21 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who did Paul and his companions go to lodge with in Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: Mnason of Cyprus
questions.explanation: This is stated in Acts 21:16, where Mnason is mentioned as the one with whom they should lodge.

questions.question: What does Acts 21:17 promise will happen if the brethren receive Paul and his companions gladly?
options: They will ask for a sign
questions.correctAnswer: They will glorify the Lord
questions.explanation: Acts 21:17 shows the positive reception of Paul and his companions by the brethren in Jerusalem.

questions.question: What did Paul declare to the elders in Jerusalem?
options: What God had wrought among the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: What God had wrought among the Gentiles
questions.explanation: This is found in Acts 21:19, where Paul shares what God did through his ministry among the Gentiles.

questions.question: What did the elders say when they heard Paul's report?
questions.correctAnswer: They glorified the Lord
questions.explanation: Acts 21:20 states that upon hearing Paul's report, the elders glorified the Lord.

questions.question: What were the Jews informed about Paul?
options: He forsook the law of Moses
He was a disciple of James
questions.correctAnswer: He forsook the law of Moses
questions.explanation: Acts 21:21 indicates that the Jews were informed that Paul taught Jews among Gentiles to forsake Moses.

questions.question: What did the elders suggest Paul do to prove his observance of the law?
options: Take a vow with four men
questions.correctAnswer: Take a vow with four men
questions.explanation: Acts 21:23 shows that the elders advised Paul to take a vow with four men to demonstrate his adherence to the law.

questions.question: What did the elders conclude regarding Gentile believers?
options: They should follow all Jewish customs
They should not be troubled with the law
questions.correctAnswer: They should not be troubled with the law
questions.explanation: Acts 21:25 specifies that the Gentiles were instructed to observe no such things as the law.

questions.question: What action did Paul take with the men regarding their vow?
options: He took them and purified himself
questions.correctAnswer: He took them and purified himself
questions.explanation: Acts 21:26 describes Paul taking the men and purifying himself with them.

questions.question: What happened when the seven days of purification were almost ended?
options: The Jews from Asia stirred up the people
questions.correctAnswer: The Jews from Asia stirred up the people
questions.explanation: Acts 21:27 shows that Jews from Asia stirred up the people against Paul.

questions.question: What accusation did the Jews make against Paul?
options: He brought Greeks into the temple
questions.correctAnswer: He brought Greeks into the temple
questions.explanation: In Acts 21:28, the Jews accused Paul of bringing Greeks into the temple and polluting the holy place.

questions.question: How did Paul respond to the warnings about going to Jerusalem?
options: He expressed readiness to die for Jesus
He decided to leave the ministry
questions.correctAnswer: He expressed readiness to die for Jesus
questions.explanation: Acts 21:13 shows Paul expressing his willingness to face death rather than avoid going to Jerusalem.

questions.question: What was the reaction of Paul’s companions when they heard Agabus's prophecy?
options: They begged him not to go
questions.correctAnswer: They begged him not to go
questions.explanation: Acts 21:12 states that both Paul’s companions and those from that place besought him not to go up to Jerusalem after hearing Agabus's prophecy.

questions.question: True or False: The brethren in Jerusalem received Paul and his companions with joy.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 21:17 confirms that the brethren received Paul and his companions gladly.

questions.question: True or False: Paul taught that all Jews must forsake the customs of Moses.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 21:21 mentions that Paul was accused of teaching Jews to forsake Moses, but he did not teach this; he upheld the law.

questions.question: True or False: The Jews from Asia did not recognize Paul in the temple.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 21:27 shows that the Jews from Asia recognized Paul and stirred up the people against him.

hard.title: Acts Chapter 21 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 21.

questions.question: Who was the Ephesian man that the Jews supposed Paul had brought into the temple?
questions.correctAnswer: Trophimus
questions.explanation: Acts 21:29 states they had seen with Paul in the city Trophimus an Ephesian, whom they supposed Paul brought into the temple.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the city when the Jews accused Paul of bringing a Gentile into the temple?
options: All the city was moved and people ran together
Paul was immediately arrested without uproar
questions.correctAnswer: All the city was moved and people ran together
questions.explanation: Acts 21:30 describes how all the city was moved and people ran together, took Paul, and drew him out of the temple.

questions.question: What did the chief captain do when he heard that all Jerusalem was in an uproar?
options: Took soldiers and centurions and ran down to them
Called for a city council meeting
Sent a letter to the governor
questions.correctAnswer: Took soldiers and centurions and ran down to them
questions.explanation: Acts 21:32 states the chief captain immediately took soldiers and centurions and ran down to the people causing the uproar.

questions.question: How was Paul bound when the chief captain arrested him?
options: With iron shackles on one hand
questions.correctAnswer: With two chains
questions.explanation: Acts 21:33 says the chief captain took Paul and commanded him to be bound with two chains.

questions.question: What language did Paul use to address the crowd when given permission to speak?
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrew
questions.explanation: Acts 21:40 records Paul spoke to the people in the Hebrew tongue after being given license by the chief captain.

questions.question: Who did the chief captain mistake Paul for when he asked, 'Art not thou that Egyptian'?
options: An Egyptian who led four thousand murderers into the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: An Egyptian who led four thousand murderers into the wilderness
questions.explanation: Acts 21:38 shows the chief captain thought Paul was the Egyptian who previously led four thousand murderers into the wilderness.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'ektos' (ἐκτός) in Acts 21:28, meaning 'outside' or 'excluded', signify in the context of the temple?
questions.correctAnswer: Outside the temple precincts
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'ektos' in Acts 21:28 refers to being 'outside' the temple precincts, indicating Gentiles were excluded from sacred areas.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in Acts 21:11 when Agabus binds his own hands and feet as a prophecy of Paul's arrest?
questions.correctAnswer: Mime or symbolic action
questions.explanation: Acts 21:11 uses a mime or symbolic action where Agabus physically acts out Paul's future binding, a prophetic sign-act.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed in Paul's statement about being ready to be bound and die for Jesus in Acts 21:13?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 116:16
questions.explanation: Psalm 116:16 speaks of the preciousness of being bound in the Lord’s sight, echoing Paul's readiness for suffering in Acts 21:13.

questions.question: The uproar and accusations against Paul in Acts 21:27-30 parallel which New Testament event involving Stephen?
options: Peter’s sermon at Pentecost in Acts 2
questions.correctAnswer: Stephen’s stoning in Acts 7
questions.explanation: The violent uproar and accusations against Paul in Acts 21:27-30 parallel the hostile crowd accusing and stoning Stephen in Acts 7.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes the uproar in the temple described in Acts 21:30?
options: Paul’s purification with the four men who had a vow
questions.correctAnswer: Paul’s purification with the four men who had a vow
questions.explanation: Acts 21:26 describes Paul purifying himself with four men who had a vow just before the Jews of Asia saw him in the temple, leading to the uproar in Acts 21:30.

questions.question: How does Paul's identification as a 'Jew of Tarsus' in Acts 21:39 serve as a rhetorical device?
options: It asserts his Roman citizenship and cultural sophistication
questions.correctAnswer: It asserts his Roman citizenship and cultural sophistication
questions.explanation: In Acts 21:39 Paul’s claim to be a Jew of Tarsus, a notable city, highlights his cultural and legal status, countering the Egyptian rebel's image.

questions.question: In Acts 21:37-38, the chief captain's question about Paul's ability to speak Greek highlights what cultural-historical reality?
options: Greek was the lingua franca of the eastern Roman Empire
Latin was the common language among Jews
Aramaic was the language of the Roman soldiers
questions.correctAnswer: Greek was the lingua franca of the eastern Roman Empire
questions.explanation: Acts 21:37-38 shows the captain’s surprise Paul spoke Greek, reflecting Greek’s role as the common language in the eastern Roman Empire.

questions.question: How does the scene of Paul being carried by soldiers due to the violence of the people (Acts 21:35) function as a typology in biblical narrative?
options: It prefigures the passion of Christ carried to crucifixion
It symbolizes the Exodus from Egypt
It represents the fall of Jerusalem
It illustrates the journey of Jonah
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the passion of Christ carried to crucifixion
questions.explanation: Paul being borne by soldiers amidst violent opposition (Acts 21:35) typologically echoes Christ’s passion where he was carried to crucifixion.

questions.question: True or False: In Acts 21:34, the chief captain immediately understood the reason for the uproar and released Paul.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 21:34 explains the chief captain could not understand the uproar's reason and commanded Paul to be taken into the castle.

theological.title: Acts Chapter 21 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 21 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 21:4 teach about the guidance of the Holy Spirit in the lives of believers?
options: The Holy Spirit directs believers away from danger
The Holy Spirit only convicts of sin, not directs
The Holy Spirit is primarily a comforter during trials
The Holy Spirit reveals future events to all believers
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Spirit directs believers away from danger
questions.explanation: Acts 21:4 shows that the disciples, through the Spirit, told Paul not to go to Jerusalem, indicating the Spirit’s guidance in decision-making.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christian suffering and perseverance is taught in Acts 21:13?
options: Believers should be willing to suffer and even die for Christ
Persecution is a sign of God’s disfavor
Faith guarantees freedom from physical harm
Suffering is to be avoided at all costs
questions.correctAnswer: Believers should be willing to suffer and even die for Christ
questions.explanation: Paul expresses readiness not only to be bound but also to die for Jesus’ name, teaching the doctrine of willing sacrifice for the Gospel (Acts 21:13).

questions.question: What doctrine about the unity of Jewish and Gentile believers is reflected in Acts 21:25?
options: Gentile believers are not bound by the Mosaic Law except certain prohibitions
Gentiles must fully observe the Mosaic Law to be saved
Jewish believers must forsake the Law to accept Gentiles
Salvation is through works of the Law for all believers
questions.correctAnswer: Gentile believers are not bound by the Mosaic Law except certain prohibitions
questions.explanation: Acts 21:25 clarifies that Gentiles are free from the Law except to abstain from idolatry, blood, strangled animals, and fornication, affirming doctrinal distinction in law observance.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 21:11 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience
questions.explanation: Agabus, inspired by the Holy Ghost, correctly predicts Paul's binding, illustrating God's attribute of omniscience (Acts 21:11).

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted by the believers’ response in Acts 21:14 when they say, 'The will of the Lord be done'?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Their submission to God's will despite danger demonstrates recognition of God's sovereign control over events (Acts 21:14).

questions.question: How does Acts 21:20–21 prepare the theme of Jewish-Christian relations found throughout the New Testament?
options: It reveals tensions regarding the Law and Gentile inclusion
It shows full harmony between Jewish and Gentile believers
It denies any necessity of the Law for Jewish believers
It promotes the abolition of Jewish customs
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals tensions regarding the Law and Gentile inclusion
questions.explanation: The elders' concern about Paul's teaching that Jews among Gentiles forsake Moses reflects ongoing tension about Law observance and Gentile believers (Acts 21:20-21).

questions.question: In what way does Paul’s willingness to be bound and die in Acts 21:13 connect to the theme of Christ’s own passion in Scripture?
options: It parallels the suffering servant motif of Jesus
It rejects the necessity of suffering for righteousness
It emphasizes human effort over divine grace
questions.correctAnswer: It parallels the suffering servant motif of Jesus
questions.explanation: Paul’s readiness to suffer echoes Christ’s own passion and the call to take up the cross, fulfilling the theme of redemptive suffering (Acts 21:13).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Acts 21:23 and Acts 21:26 teach about the relationship between Jewish law and Christian liberty?
options: Observing the Law can be a voluntary act to maintain peace among believers
Christians are strictly bound to all ceremonial laws
Gentiles must be circumcised to be saved
Law observance is irrelevant and discouraged for all
questions.correctAnswer: Observing the Law can be a voluntary act to maintain peace among believers
questions.explanation: Paul purifying himself with men under a vow shows voluntary Law observance to dispel misunderstandings, highlighting liberty used for unity (Acts 21:23,26).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 21:4 and Acts 21:12 teach about human responsibility and divine sovereignty?
options: Believers may receive divine warnings but must ultimately submit to God's sovereign will
Believers can override the Spirit's warnings by human will
Warnings from the Spirit guarantee outcomes
questions.correctAnswer: Believers may receive divine warnings but must ultimately submit to God's sovereign will
questions.explanation: The disciples warn Paul not to go, but after he insists, they submit to the Lord’s will, showing the balance of human responsibility and divine sovereignty (Acts 21:4,12).

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of false accusations and persecution is taught by Acts 21:27-30?
options: Believers may suffer persecution based on false charges and misunderstanding
Persecution only comes from personal sin
The church should retaliate against persecutors
questions.correctAnswer: Believers may suffer persecution based on false charges and misunderstanding
questions.explanation: The Jews accuse Paul falsely, stirring the crowd to violence, showing how believers suffer from misunderstandings (Acts 21:27-30).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Acts 21:26–31 shows Paul deceiving the Jewish leaders by pretending to keep the Law. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Paul voluntarily participates in Jewish purification rites to demonstrate respect for the Law
Paul rejects the Law entirely and deceives the leaders
Paul avoids all Jewish customs to provoke the crowd
Paul uses the Law for personal gain
questions.correctAnswer: Paul voluntarily participates in Jewish purification rites to demonstrate respect for the Law
questions.explanation: Paul purifies himself with men under a vow to prove he observes the Law, not to deceive (Acts 21:26-31).

questions.question: What doctrine about the prophetic role in the early church is illustrated by Acts 21:10-11?
options: Prophets serve to warn and confirm God’s plans for believers
Prophecy is only about future predictions unrelated to present events
Prophecy is less important than apostolic teaching
The prophetic gift ceased after the apostles
questions.correctAnswer: Prophets serve to warn and confirm God’s plans for believers
questions.explanation: Agabus’s prophecy warns Paul of coming imprisonment, showing prophecy’s role in guidance (Acts 21:10-11).

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by the brethren receiving Paul gladly in Jerusalem according to Acts 21:17?
questions.correctAnswer: Love
questions.explanation: The brethren's glad reception of Paul reflects God's attribute of love among the body of Christ (Acts 21:17).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 21:19 and 21:20 teach about God’s work among Gentiles and Jewish believers’ zeal for the Law?
options: God works powerfully among Gentiles, yet Jewish believers remain zealous for the Law
Gentiles replace Jewish believers in God’s plan
Jewish believers abandon the Law when Gentiles believe
God rejects Jewish zeal for the Law
questions.correctAnswer: God works powerfully among Gentiles, yet Jewish believers remain zealous for the Law
questions.explanation: Paul reports God’s work among Gentiles, and the elders affirm Jewish believers’ zeal for the Law, showing coexistence (Acts 21:19-20).

questions.question: How does Acts 21:39 illustrate the doctrine of Christian identity in relation to worldly citizenship and heritage?
options: Christian identity transcends ethnic and civic backgrounds, though these remain part of personal history
Christian identity is defined solely by earthly citizenship
Ethnic background is irrelevant to Christian witness
Christian identity rejects all worldly ties
questions.correctAnswer: Christian identity transcends ethnic and civic backgrounds, though these remain part of personal history
questions.explanation: Paul identifies as a Jew and Tarsus citizen but speaks as a Christian, showing that Christian identity goes beyond ethnicity and citizenship (Acts 21:39).
